historical_context: The 10.5cm leFH 18 was the standard German divisional field howitzer. Artillerie-Regiment 33 had two light battalions (I. and II. Abteilung) with 12 guns each. Motorized for mobile operations with Panzer divisions.

leFH 18 105mm.notes: Standard German divisional artillery. Reliable and effective.

strengths: Excellent HE round for infantry support
weaknesses: Not effective in anti-tank role (HE only)
tactical_notes.typical_deployment: Provide indirect fire support for Panzer and infantry attacks. Suppressive fire on British defensive positions. Counter-battery fire against British 25-pdrs. Smoke screens for advancing armor. Mobile enough to keep pace with Panzer divisions. German doctrine emphasized massed artillery fire at decisive points.

HE.description: High explosive for infantry and soft targets

phase_6_data_source.battalions: I. Abteilung (12 guns), II. Abteilung (12 guns)
phase_6_data_source.organization: Each battalion has 3 batteries of 4 guns each
phase_6_data_source.notes: Motorized light howitzer battalions. Regiment also had III. Abteilung with 150mm heavy howitzers.

historical_engagements.operation_battleaxe: June 15-17, 1941. German artillery provided fire support for defensive operations and counter-attacks. Coordinated with 88mm FlaK guns.
historical_engagements.effectiveness: Effective in supporting combined arms defense. Worked with armor and anti-tank guns to defeat British attacks.
